To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the resolution of 29Si MAS spectra can be improved by a factor of ∼10 over previous values by careful optimization of the experimental conditions.

(a) the most highly siliceous samples of the most highly crystallized ZSM-5 are the only ones that give rise to ultra-high resolution spectra; (b) this resolution is achieved only when the experimental variables are optimized, and the most important of these are the sample temperature and the spinning rate; (c) the resolution is largely independent of the sample temperature and is maintained in the presence of sorbates; and (d) the resolution is limited by the natural linewidth of
the 29Si MAS spectrum of a completely siliceous ZSM-5 zeolite, prepared by a new method, is the most highly resolved spectrum of a solid ever reported.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization, and catalytic properties of highly siliceously zeolites and zeolite-like materials.

the development of ultra-high resolution 1H and 29Si magic- angle spinning nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the study of zeolites and related materials, and with the use of this new technique to obtain new information on the structures of zeolites.
the preparation, characterization, and catalytic properties of new microporous materials with high silica contents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, with a combination of the best available materials and a very careful optimization of the experimental conditions, ultra-high resolution can be achieved in the 29Si NMR of rigid crystalline materials.
the 29Si MAS spectrum of a highly siliceous ZSM-5 sample is the best 29Si spectrum yet recorded for any crystalline material.
the spectra are the best ever recorded for any crystalline material, and are of a quality that was thought impossible to attain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

it has been demonstrated that it is now possible to obtain high resolution solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectra for highly siliceous crystalline materials, and that this is a powerful new tool in zeolite characterization.
the 29Si MAS spectra of highly silicious zeolites are now as clear as the 13C spectra of aliphatic compounds.

the spectra are of such high quality that they can be regarded as a definitive fingerprint for zeolite ZSMS, and it is anticipated that the same high quality will be obtained with other highly siliceous materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with care, ultra-high resolution can be obtained for rigid crystalline samples, which should be of general interest to those working on the structure of crystalline solids.

the 29Si NMR spectra are very sensitive to small changes in framework structure, and that the resolution can be optimized to the point that it can be used to identify the numbers of lattice positions in the framework of zeolites and zeotypes.

it is possible to obtain ultra-high resolution 1H and 13C NMR spectra from highly crystalline materials and that the resolution can be improved by a factor of 5-10 over the best results obtained previously. © 2005 Elsevier
